newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel warns Syria over nerve gas report.
newsitem.headline: Israel warns Syria over nerve gas report.

text.p: Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy warned Syria on Tuesday over its reported manufacture of a more lethal nerve gas, saying Israel had means many times more destructive at its disposal.

Levy, asked to respond to a report by the Israel daily Haaretz that Syria was manufacturing a nerve gas that acts via the skin and is hard to disperse, said Israel was "following a development like that and other developments".
"Anyone who does this understands also that we have possibilities over and above what the other side can imagine," he added.
"But it must be seen that not by intimidation do we further the peace process but rather by a realistic process of direct negotiations which the Syrians are still refusing," Levy said.

Haaretz's respected military analyst Zeev Schiff, quoting Western intelligence sources, said Syria was making a gas called VX and was in the initial stages of preparing warheads for ground-to-ground missiles that could deliver it.
The Syrians already have Sarin gas which acts via the respiratory system, Schiff wrote. "But this time they've entered a new area, a new gas named VX," he told Israel Radio.
Levy said Israel would continue with "the vital things that we are also developing...for the purpose of deterence".
The "other side", he said, must understand that "it alone does not control something serious like this but that we also control things that are seven times more serious".
Israel has declined comment over the years on news reports in France and elsewhere that a facility in a suburb of Tel Aviv is working on biological and chemical weapons.

Also according to foreign news reports, Israel has a nuclear arsenal of at least 200 bombs. Israel's only comment on the nuclear option is that it will not be the first to introduce nuclear weapons to the Middle East.
Israel-Syria peace talks ground to a halt at the beginning of 1996 under Israel's previous Labour-led government.

In May, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of the right-wing Likud party was elected after a campaign in which he insisted Israel must keep the Golan Heights it captured from Syria in 1967. Damascus demands a full Israeli withdrawal.
